stem: Which of the following best describes the anatomical location and pathophysiology of bronchiolitis?

options.text: Inflammation of the larynx and trachea resulting in subglottic narrowing.
Inflammation and edema of the airways approximately $\frac{2}{3}$ down the bronchial tree causing narrowing.
Infiltration of inflammatory cells primarily in the alveoli causing consolidation.
Chronic narrowing of the large airways due to structural abnormalities.

explanation: Bronchiolitis involves inflammation of the smaller bronchioles deep in the lungs, leading to cell necrosis and mucus production.
rationale: Consider the specific part of the bronchial tree mentioned in the definitions and the resulting physical changes.

optionExplanations.A: This description refers to the pathology of croup, which affects the upper and middle segments of the respiratory tree.
optionExplanations.B: Bronchiolitis involves inflammation of the smaller bronchioles deep in the lungs, leading to cell necrosis and mucus production.
optionExplanations.C: This describes pneumonia, which is a common differential diagnosis but distinct from the airway inflammation seen in bronchiolitis.
optionExplanations.D: Bronchiolitis is an acute inflammatory illness caused by a virus, not a chronic structural abnormality like tracheomalacia.
